title: `podIdentity.provider: azure` (AAD Pod Identity) and `aws-kiam` are deprecated — removed in 2.15
quote: Remove support for Azure AD Pod Identity-based authentication (#5035)
remediation: AAD Pod Identity is archived by Microsoft and KIAM is abandoned; KEDA announces both removals here (they land in 2.15, where the CRD enum no longer accepts the values). On each TriggerAuthentication / ClusterTriggerAuthentication named — including a `podIdentity` block nested under `azureKeyVault`, `awsSecretManager` or `gcpSecretManager` — switch `azure` to `azure-workload` (Azure AD Workload Identity) and `aws-kiam` to `aws` (IRSA / EKS Pod Identity).
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .podIdentity? // empty | .provider] | any(. == "azure" or . == "aws-kiam")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) providers=\([.. | objects | .podIdentity? // empty | .provider] | unique | join(","))"'  # each row still uses a provider 2.15 removes
coversNotes: docs concepts/authentication.md: DEPRECATED: This will be removed in KEDA v2.15

title: `podIdentity.provider: aws-eks` is deprecated — removal announced for KEDA v3
quote: WARNING:** `aws-eks` auth has been deprecated and support for…** — ⚠️ **WARNING:** `aws-eks` auth has been deprecated and support for it will be removed from KEDA on v3. We strongly encourage the migration to `aws` auth.
remediation: Announced in the docs and GitHub discussion #5343 only — no CHANGELOG entry. Each TriggerAuthentication / ClusterTriggerAuthentication named keeps working through every 2.x release; move it to `podIdentity.provider: aws` (IRSA / EKS Pod Identity, with `roleArn` on the TriggerAuthentication instead of `awsRoleArn` on the trigger) before v3.
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .podIdentity? // empty | .provider] | any(. == "aws-eks")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row uses the aws-eks provider slated for removal in v3
coversNotes: docs concepts/authentication.md: DEPRECATED: This will be removed in KEDA v3

title: AWS scalers: `identityOwner` is deprecated as of 2.13 — removal announced for KEDA v3

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned; apache-kafka, prometheus (AWS SigV4) and, from 2.15, kafka read it through the same GetAwsAuthorization

quote: `identityOwner` - Receive permissions on the SQS Queue via Pod Identity or from the KEDA operator itself (see below). (DEPRECATED: This parameter is deprecated as of KEDA v2.13 and will be removed in version `3`, Values: `pod`, `operator`, Default: `pod`, Optional, This field only applies for `aws-eks` and `aws-kiam` authentications)
remediation: Docs-only deprecation (no CHANGELOG entry). `identityOwner: operator|pod` only applies to the `aws-eks` / `aws-kiam` pod identities; with `podIdentity.provider: aws` the TriggerAuthentication's `identityOwner` decides. Each trigger named keeps working through 2.x; drop the key when its authentication moves to `aws`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type | test("^(aws-|apache-kafka$|kafka$|prometheus$)")) and (.metadata // {} | has("identityOwner"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type) identityOwner=\(.metadata.identityOwner)"'  # each row carries the trigger-level key the docs deprecate

title: AWS scalers: the `awsRoleArn` authentication parameter is deprecated — it only applies to `aws-eks` pod identity

detection.reason: `awsRoleArn` has only ever been read from authParams — a TriggerAuthentication `secretTargetRef[]`/`env[]` entry with `parameter: awsRoleArn` (aws_common.go v2.13.0:93,106) — and the projection carries the authentication block KEY NAMES and counts, not parameter names

quote: `awsRoleArn` - Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) uniquely identify AWS resource. (This field is deprecated only applies for `aws-eks` and `aws-kiam` authentications, for `aws` is set in the auth)
remediation: For each AWS scaler named, read the TriggerAuthentication its trigger references: an entry mapping `parameter: awsRoleArn` is the deprecated path (it only applies to `aws-eks` pod identity, itself deprecated). Switch the TriggerAuthentication to `podIdentity.provider: aws` with `roleArn` set, or to static credentials via `awsAccessKeyID`/`awsSecretAccessKey` parameters; under provider `aws` the authParams value is still honoured for now (v2.13.0:92-94).
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([(.spec.secretTargetRef // [])[], (.spec.env // [])[] | .parameter] | index("awsRoleArn") != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row maps a parameter to awsRoleArn — the deprecated aws-eks path

title: Azure Data Explorer no longer reads `clientSecret` from trigger metadata — and `clientSecretFromEnv` is broken from 2.13.0

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **General**: Clean up previously deprecated code in Azure Data Explorer Scaler about clientSecret for 2.13 release (#5051)
remediation: Move the secret to a TriggerAuthentication `clientSecret` parameter. Do NOT switch to `clientSecretFromEnv`: from 2.13.0 the scaler assigns the environment-variable NAME as the secret (azure_data_explorer_scaler.go v2.13.0:166-167, a regression from 2.12.1's getParameterFromConfig), so that path fails authentication too; 2.20 only changes its error text.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "azure-data-explorer")) | select(((.metadata // {}) | has("clientSecret") or has("clientSecretFromEnv"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row carries the secret in trigger metadata (or the broken FromEnv path) — move it to a TriggerAuthentication

title: The 2.13 CRDs reject `podIdentity.provider: none` — the documented default is missing from the first enum

detection.reason: checked on every podIdentity.provider value the agent projects, at any depth (top level and under the secret-store blocks)

quote: enum: - azure - azure-workload - gcp - aws - aws-eks - aws-kiam
remediation: While the 2.13.0/2.13.1 CRDs are installed, any UPDATE of a TriggerAuthentication or ClusterTriggerAuthentication that keeps `podIdentity.provider: none` (the documented default, keda.sh/docs/2.12/concepts/authentication) is rejected by the schema — the first enum omits it; v2.14.0 restores it (ef1074a4c, #5593). Remove the `podIdentity` block (equivalent to `none`) before the hop, or upgrade straight through to 2.14.0 or later. Existing objects keep working until edited.
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .podIdentity? | objects | .provider] | index("none") != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row sets provider: none somewhere — its next edit is rejected by the 2.13 CRDs
